subject: Packaging options for Pathwell pilot — phased commit & rollback
messages:

Subject: Packaging options for Pathwell pilot — requirements attached

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Pathwell's engineering and product leads reviewed Redwood's throughput and cost profile and we have a few packaging questions before we lock in a pilot:

- We're planning a 6-week pilot that will start at ~10% of our prod traffic, with the option to scale to 40% if latency holds. Can you outline upgrade steps if we need to increase throughput mid-pilot?
- If we later decide to step down, what does the downgrade path look like (credits, notice period, re-assignment of seats)?
- We want bundling visibility: is observability (token-level latency/cost), KV caching, and model-variant fallback part of any add-on bundle or only enterprise tiers?
- Pricing: curious about short-term pilot pricing vs. annual commit discounts and what exceptions you can offer for pilots that convert to Dedicated capacity.

I've attached our short requirements doc (pathwell_requirements.pdf). Can you send a clear, stepwise option set (pilot -> scale -> commit -> rollback) and any exemplar numbers/discounts you can offer? Procurement is on the thread for the commercial detail.

Thanks,
Sam Todd

Hi Sam — great to meet yesterday and thanks for the requirements doc. High level below; attaching a spreadsheet with pricing scenarios and the pilot checklist.

Option A — Standard Pilot (no reserved capacity)
- Start: Hosted API, auto-batched, prefix/KV caching enabled.
- Scale: increase rate limits and routing to higher-capacity nodes; no long-term commitment required.
- Downgrade: immediate — no credits since there's no reserved capacity; stop scaling and traffic routes back to baseline.
- Good when you want minimal ops and a short evaluation window.

Option B — Pilot with Burstable Reserved (recommended for 40% headroom)
- Start: 30-day reserved pool sized for expected peak (pro-rated charge for pilot).
- Scale: we can double reserved pool mid-pilot with a 72-hr notice; billing is pro-rated for the additional reserved units.
- Downgrade: 30-day notice to reduce reserved pool; pro-rated credits applied to the next invoice for the unused reserved period.
- This gives capacity predictability and easier SLA guarantees.

Option C — Commit & Convert (Annual Dedicated)
- Annual commit, 10% discount baseline for 12-month; larger discounts available with higher commits.
- Includes observability bundle (longer retention), model-variant fallback config, and KMS integration on higher tiers.

Feature bundling notes
- Observability (token-level breakdown), KV caching, and model fallback are included in Dedicated and in the higher pilot-with-burst tier as an add-on bundle.
- Labs features (advanced quant profiles) are separate optional add-ons.

Discounts & conversion path
- Pilot -> Dedicated conversion: we can credit pilot reserved pro-rated spend toward the annual commitment up to the value of the pilot charges.
- For converting pilots we typically offer a one-time conversion credit (example sheet shows 15% of pilot reserved spend as credit toward year 1 for >6-month expected consumption).

Next steps
1) Please confirm expected average QPS and 95th p90 latency requirements in the attached sheet.
2) We'll send a pilot commercial term sheet (simple SOW) with the pro-rate/downgrade excerpt.
3) If Procurement prefers, Ben can share standard reserved capacity language and the explicit downgrade credit calculation.

Attached: redwood_packaging_options_v1.xlsx (Attachment: pricing scenarios, stepwise flows)

— Irene

Irene / Ben — thanks for the clear options. Two quick clarifications from Procurement/Product:

1) Downgrade credits: can you confirm the mechanics precisely? If we reduce reserved capacity after 30 days, does Redwood issue a credit on the next invoice (value = unused reserved days * reserved rate), or is it applied as future spend only? We prefer an on-invoice credit to simplify our accounting.

2) SLA & data residency: for the Burstable Reserved pilot we need an SLA statement (target p99 latency and uptime) and confirmation that logs/telemetry remain in our US region with the same retention as Dedicated (30 days) — is that included or an add-on?

3) Conversion discount: the 15% pilot-to-year credit example looks reasonable. Can you send a sample calculation using the numbers in our requirements doc (I've highlighted expected peak/reserve numbers)?

If you can send the short terms excerpt and sample calc today we can loop Legal & Procurement and get a PO out within the week.

— Sam

Hi Sam — quick answers inline and attaching the exact excerpt from our reserved-capacity terms.

On your questions:
1) Downgrade credits — mechanics:
- If you reduce reserved capacity mid-term we calculate unused reserved days * reserved unit rate and issue a credit on the next invoice. For pilots we can expedite that to be visible on the same billing cycle if requested (accounting lead time may vary by payment method).

2) SLA & data residency:
- Burstable Reserved pilot: we can commit to the same regional telemetry retention (30 days) and keep logs in the US region for Pathwell. SLA: for reserved capacity we provide an uptime target of 99.5% and p99 latency targets in the SOW (we'll add your p99 target from the requirements doc). For hosted non-reserved pilots there is no SLA.

3) Sample calculation — attached to the pricing spreadsheet (redwood_packaging_options_v1.xlsx) we added a sample calc row using your highlighted numbers; summary: pilot reserved spend of $12,000 over 30 days -> potential conversion credit example = $1,800 (15%). Exact credit adjusts by final commit size.

Attached: downgrade_terms_excerpt.txt (text) — excerpted language you can drop into your procurement doc.

If that works, Irene and I can turn the pilot SOW into a PO-ready doc and route for signature.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
